proposed_from.topic: Measurement design as the argument of the semiparametric efficiency bound for long-term treatment effects. Setting: the Imbens-Kallus-Mao-Wang long-term data-combination model (arXiv:2202.07234, JRSS-B 2025) verbatim -- an observational sample observing short-term outcomes and the long-term outcome but confounded by a latent variable, an experimental sample with randomized treatment and short-term outcomes but no long-term outcome, external validity, the sequential-outcome restriction, and the two completeness conditions -- with target the long-term average treatment effect in the observational population. New primitive the anchor lacks: a finite catalogue of candidate short-term outcomes with per-variable measurement costs, a per-unit cost for an experimental unit and a higher one for a long-term-follow-up unit, a per-unit measurement-cost cap, and an ex-ante-known admissible family of (measured subset, role-assignment) pairs, every member of which is assumed regular. Focal object: the design-value function, the budget-normalized local semiparametric efficiency bound for the long-term ATE indexed by the measurement design, defined as infinity off the regular set, and its profile over the budget allocation between the two samples. Open content: whether selecting short-term proxies by their predictive power for the long-term outcome carries any finite efficiency guarantee. The conjecture is that it does not -- that over a non-degenerate region of laws no predictive optimizer is design-value optimal and the worst-case ratio of the design value at a predictive optimizer to the design-value minimum over the admissible family is unbounded, with every admissible design regular so that the failure is efficiency and not identification -- together with the positive side, that the design-value gap on the admissible family is the correct selection criterion, is identified by a full-catalogue pilot, and yields a feasible plug-in measurement-design rule. Prior art leaves this open: the anchor and the surrogate-index literature take the measured proxy system and the sampling ratio as exogenously given, published surrogate efficiency results compare with versus without a given surrogate set rather than optimizing over sets, and existing optimal-measurement-design results cover only linear front-door and Gaussian instrumental-variable models or optimize two-phase sampling probabilities for a fixed measured variable set. The anchor itself reports, without explanation, that its estimator can perform worse as surrogates are added, and attributes this to bridge non-uniqueness.

seed_list: Predictive proxy selection has no finite approximation guarantee for the profiled bridge-model efficiency bound on a relatively open regular region.
The two source-specific canonical-gradient variances generate an exact cost-optimal sample-allocation profile for every subset-role design.
A full-catalogue pilot consistently selects the value-minimizing measurement design and preserves independent-main-sample Wald inference.
Near-tie measurement selection has a minimax design-regret frontier indexed by pilot size and bridge ill-posedness.
Nonunique bridge solution sets admit a minimum-norm canonical-gradient characterization that orders measurement designs.
Uniform inverse-operator comparability yields a finite prediction-to-efficiency approximation constant.
Online allocation across experimental and follow-up sources attains zero regret with design-specific conditional moments.
Joint long-term policy learning and proxy measurement selection admits a welfare-regret frontier.
Symmetry inversion yields finite-sample post-selection intervals after proxy-design choice.
Adding a predictive proxy has an exact frontier for improving or worsening efficiency under sequential role reassignment.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Does selecting short-term outcomes by predictive accuracy have any finite approximation guarantee for the budget-normalized semiparametric efficiency bound when every candidate design is regular?
seed_details.anchor_read: The introduction, pages 362--365, poses persistent confounding and motivates sequential short-term roles; Theorem 4 and the nonuniqueness remark, pages 378--380, give the fixed-system bound; the conclusion, page 386, calls the internal structure of repeated short-term outcomes largely unexplored.
adjacent_threads: CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 proves prediction-efficiency equivalence for ordinary randomized covariate collection.
KallusMao2025 compares efficiency with and without a fixed surrogate vector.
LalImbensHull2026 studies regularized combination and naive screening in a linear many-noisy-proxy model.
MareisDrton2026 optimizes partial measurement in a multivariate linear front-door model.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 because precision-optimal variable selection is equivalent to outcome prediction.
seed_details.rebuttal: That equivalence uses ordinary randomized regression adjustment; here prediction risk controls neither of two inverse bridge operators, the role assignment, nor the source-specific canonical-gradient variances.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: What is the cost-optimal allocation between randomized short-term units and observational long-term-follow-up units for each regular measurement design?
seed_details.anchor_read: The estimation section fixes \(n_E/n_O\to\lambda\), and Theorems 2--4 display separate experimental and observational variance contributions; the conclusion does not optimize \(\lambda\).
adjacent_threads: GuptaLiptonChilders2024 optimizes costed frequencies across generic moment sources.
WangWangMiao2023 minimizes a two-phase semiparametric bound for a fixed measured-variable system.
TaoZengLin2020 derives efficiency-optimal phase-two sampling probabilities in fixed regression models.
seed_details.red_team: The square-root allocation is immediate Neyman allocation once the two variances are displayed.
seed_details.rebuttal: The algebra is elementary, but the publishable object jointly profiles source costs and a finite family of nonnested subset-role bridge models and feeds the pilot selector; it is retained as a supporting angle rather than the sole kernel.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Can a full-catalogue pilot learn the best subset-role design with vanishing design-value regret and valid long-term ATE inference?
seed_details.anchor_read: The introduction treats source collection as a sequential decision and proves zero pointwise asymptotic-MSE regret; the conclusion explicitly leaves conditional-moment restrictions and uniform analysis open.
adjacent_threads: WangWangMiao2023 estimates a two-phase optimal rule from a pilot with one supplied full-data influence function.
CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 selects covariates and sample size from pre-experimental data and flags finite-pilot overfitting.
BennettKallusMaoNeweySyrgkanisUehara2023 supplies stable penalized minimax estimation for ill-posed conditional moments.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from generic finite-model selection plus sample splitting.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform pilot evaluation must estimate a different pair of ill-posed bridge equations and a different canonical gradient for every candidate, which fixed-influence-function pilot designs do not cover.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: What is the minimax pilot-size rate for selecting among bridge-defined measurement designs near efficiency ties?
seed_details.anchor_read: The introduction derives model-free efficiency-optimal phase-two rules from a pilot, and the discussion limits the theory to a fixed-dimensional target and a supplied full-data influence function.
seed_details.red_team: The lower bound is a generic best-arm identification result with bridge notation attached.
seed_details.rebuttal: A credible result would have to derive the observation modulus from design-specific inverse operators, but the current substrate does not yet isolate a non-generic bridge modulus.
seed_details.status: dropped after deep scan because the bridge-specific lower-bound geometry is not yet sharp

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: How should the canonical gradient be characterized when bridge functions are nonunique, and how does that change design ordering?
seed_details.anchor_read: The introduction defines strong identification of a functional despite weakly identified nuisance solutions; the conclusion leaves nonlinear functionals and partial identification open, but does not compute the two-sample long-term canonical gradient.
seed_details.red_team: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgenTchetgen2023 already supplies regular asymptotically linear proximal estimation without unique bridges.
seed_details.rebuttal: That paper does not derive the persistent-confounding two-sample efficiency bound or order costly role designs, but solving both would expand well beyond the stipulated all-designs-regular anchor model.
seed_details.status: dropped because it changes the kernel's regularity regime and dilutes measurement design

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Under what operator comparison condition does predictive selection have a finite efficiency approximation ratio?
seed_details.anchor_read: The introduction frames sample size and covariate choice as a precision-cost problem and establishes prediction equivalence; the conclusion flags pilot overfitting but not inverse-problem failure.
seed_details.red_team: A finite guarantee follows tautologically if the assumption directly bounds inverse-operator norms by predictive residual variance.
seed_details.rebuttal: The condition must be derived from primitive operator geometry rather than assume the target comparison, so this is retained only as the fallback if the impossibility construction fails.
seed_details.status: dropped as primary because the natural sufficient condition risks assuming the answer

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Can experimental and follow-up collection be adapted online when each measurement design induces conditional bridge moments?
seed_details.anchor_read: The introduction develops online moment selection with costed sources; the conclusion identifies conditional moment restrictions as a future extension.
seed_details.red_team: Once the bridge moments are supplied, the result is a direct application of online moment selection.
seed_details.rebuttal: Conditional bridge estimation adds instability, but without a new uniform limit law this remains an application rather than a distinct theorem kernel.
seed_details.status: dropped because the closest generic method substantially subsumes the allocation move

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: How should proxy measurement and treatment policy be chosen jointly for long-term welfare?
seed_details.anchor_read: The introduction targets long-term policy value with surrogate indices; the conclusion states that predictive surrogates have no policy-value guarantee and calls surrogate selection future research.
seed_details.red_team: This is the paper's stated future work and is already the natural extension of its policy-learning framework.
seed_details.rebuttal: Persistent-confounding bridges change the score, but the causal target becomes policy welfare rather than the required long-term ATE.
seed_details.status: dropped for target drift from the fixed long-term ATE

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Can symmetry inversion provide finite-sample inference after choosing a proxy design from a pilot?
seed_details.anchor_read: The paper's pilot construction and discussion provide asymptotic design guarantees but no symmetry-based inference.
seed_details.red_team: No exchangeability group maps the two-source persistent-confounding estimand into an exact randomization orbit.
seed_details.rebuttal: The obstruction holds: treatment randomization does not reveal experimental long-term outcomes, so conformal inversion has no valid finite-sample score without extra assumptions.
seed_details.status: dropped because the required symmetry is absent

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: When does adding a predictive proxy improve or worsen efficiency once the sequential role assignment can change?
seed_details.anchor_read: The introduction and conclusion show efficiency gains from a fixed predictive surrogate vector under limited outcome data; they do not compare costly role assignments or nonnested bridge operators.
seed_details.red_team: More observed variables can only weakly improve a semiparametric information bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: Role reassignment changes the statistical model and bridge operator, so candidate experiments are not nested; nevertheless an exact general frontier appears too broad without first solving the inverse-geometry separation.
seed_details.status: dropped as primary and absorbed into the predictive-impossibility handle

proposed_from.literature_map: Chosen seed: ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 fixes both the three-role short-term system and asymptotic sample ratio, while its Theorem 4 supplies two source-specific variance components and its conclusion calls repeated-outcome structure unexplored. Adjacent thread one is prediction as design: CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 proves prediction-efficiency equivalence for ordinary randomized covariates, YangEcklesDhillonAral2024 says outcome prediction need not deliver policy value, and LalImbensHull2026 shows regularization beats naive proxy screening in a distinct linear latent-surrogate model. Adjacent thread two is surrogate efficiency: KallusMao2025 compares with versus without one fixed surrogate system, not costly subsets or roles. Adjacent thread three is collection design: TaoZengLin2020 and WangWangMiao2023 optimize phase-two inclusion for fixed measured variables, GuptaLiptonChilders2024 optimizes generic source frequencies but leaves conditional moments open, and MareisDrton2026 derives a linear front-door partial-measurement policy but not nonparametric bridge-role selection. Adjacent thread four is inverse-problem inference: BennettKallusMaoNeweySyrgkanisUehara2023 and ZhangLiMiaoTchetgenTchetgen2023 handle functionals of nonunique bridge solutions, but do not compute or optimize this two-source design bound. No located paper defines \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)\) over costed subset-role designs, proves its pilot regret result, or bounds \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) in the persistent-confounding model.

banked_reason: Sound subfield result, but below the intended field bar: it compares the published CLW predictive-design selector with this note's newly defined bridge-efficient oracle benchmark rather than establishing a published-vs-published dominance result.
